questions.markdown:
(a) A mobile accessories retailer analyses six recent online orders to understand attachment behaviour around new smartphone purchases. The transaction log are shown in Table Q.1A

The product codes map to real items as follows:

a = Smartphone  
b = Protective Case  
c = Screen Protector  
d = Power Bank  
e = USB Cable

**Table Q.1A**

| Transaction ID | Items |
|---|---|
| T1 | a, b, d, e |
| T2 | b, c, e |
| T3 | a, b, d, e |
| T4 | a, b, c, e |
| T5 | a, b, c, d, e |
| T6 | b, c, d |

(b) Derive all possible frequent $k$-itemsets with minimum support count $= 3$ and following the Apriori property, list pruned itemsets at each stage.

(c) Generate a minimum of 5 possible association rules using the longest frequent $k$-itemsets and verify whether the generated rules are strong with the confidence threshold $= 60\%$.

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

questions.markdown:
A hospital laboratory claims that a new COVID testing kit correctly identifies infection 95% of the time. A researcher believes that the true accuracy is less than 95% and decides to test this claim at a 5% significance level. A random sample of $n = 50$ test results gives a sample mean accuracy of 0.93. The population standard deviation is known to be 0.04. At the 5% significance level, test whether the hospital laboratory's claim is justified. (critical value $Z_{0.05} = -1.645$).

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"

Suppose you have $L_1 = \{I_1, I_2, I_3, I_4, I_5, I_6\}$ and the following transactions:

$T_1$: $\{I_1, I_2, I_3, I_6\}$  
$T_2$: $\{I_2, I_4, I_5\}$  
$T_3$: $\{I_1, I_3, I_4, I_6\}$  
$T_4$: $\{I_2, I_3, I_5, I_6\}$

Use the hash function

$$
h(x,y) = ((order(x) \times 11) + order(y)) \bmod 10

(b) Determine bucket counts.  
(c) If **min support** $= 4$, specify which buckets are pruned and list the remaining candidate itemsets $C_2$.

questions.markdown:
A supermarket dataset has the following transactions:

$T1 = \{\text{Milk}, \text{Bread}, \text{Butter}\}$  
$T2 = \{\text{Milk}, \text{Bread}\}$  
$T3 = \{\text{Milk}, \text{Butter}\}$  
$T4 = \{\text{Bread}, \text{Butter}\}$  
$T5 = \{\text{Milk}, \text{Bread}, \text{Butter}\}$

i) Compute the support for each of the following:  
(a) $\{\text{Milk}, \text{Bread}\}$  
(b) $\{\text{Milk}, \text{Butter}\}$  
(c) $\{\text{Bread}, \text{Butter}\}$

ii) Identify which itemsets are frequent if the minimum support threshold $= 60\%$.

iii) Determine which among them are maximal frequent itemsets.

Course Outcome: "CO4"

The sales of a retail store for five consecutive weeks are as follows: 100, 110, 95, 120, 130. Compute the 3-week moving average forecast for week 6. Interpret the whether this method would be appropriate if a strong upward trend continues.

questions.markdown:
A popular online bookstore analysed 800 customer purchase transactions and obtained the following data:

| Itemset | Number of Transactions |
|---|---:|
| {Fiction Book} | 360 |
| {E-Reader} | 300 |
| {Fiction Book, E-Reader} | 180 |

(a) Calculate the pattern evaluation measures Lift and Kulc for the association rule:

Fiction Book $\to$ E-Reader

(b) Interpret what the obtained Lift and Kulc values indicate about the relationship between Fiction Book and E-Reader purchases.

Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"

questions.markdown:
A manufacturing unit tracks its quarterly production output. The data for the first four quarters are given below:

| Period (t) | Actual Production (Yt) |
|---|---:|
| Q1 | 100 |
| Q2 | 120 |
| Q3 | 130 |
| Q4 | 150 |

Use smoothing constants $= 0.2$ and $= 0.4$. Applying Holt's Method

(a) Calculate the initial Level ($L_1$) and Trend ($T_2$).  
(b) Calculate the Level ($L_2$) and Trend ($T_3$) for periods 2 and 3, respectively.  
(c) Calculate the Forecast for period 4 ($F_4$).  
(d) Differentiate between Double and triple exponential smoothing techniques.

Course Outcome: "CO5" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
